canonicalName: Hamstring Pump (lying, knee bend and straighten)
equipment: a plain dark grey exercise mat only, no other equipment
panel1: Lying on her back on the mat, the leg farthest from the camera bent with that foot flat on the mat; the leg nearest the camera lifted so the thigh points straight up at the ceiling, both hands clasped behind that thigh, and that knee BENT 90 degrees so the shin is parallel to the floor
panel2: Same position and same hand hold behind the lifted thigh, but that knee is now STRAIGHTENED so the whole lifted leg points straight up at the ceiling, foot flexed
delta: in panel 2 the held leg's knee is straightened so the foot points straight up at the ceiling
paintOn: the back of the thigh of the lifted, held leg
doNotPaint: the leg with its foot on the mat, arms, abdomen
muscleSource: Exercise demonstration linked from the USMS article (The Lifelong Athlete 'Hamstring Pumps' video); hamstrings lengthened by knee extension with the hip flexed

canonicalName: Ankle Press (pike heel press, 5 s hold)
equipment: a plain dark grey exercise mat only, no other equipment
panel1: Pike position on hands and feet like a downward dog: hands flat on the mat, arms straight, hips lifted high, legs straight, both HEELS LIFTED a hand-width off the mat on the balls of the feet
panel2: Same pike position, but both heels are PRESSED DOWN flat onto the mat and held, legs straight
delta: both heels are lifted off the mat in panel 1 and pressed flat onto the mat in panel 2
paintOn: the back of both lower legs (calves)
muscleSource: USMS article 'Exercises to help you recover from swim workouts' (ankle mobility section) + linked 'Ankle Press' demonstration video; calf lengthening by ankle dorsiflexion
poseRefNote: this photo shows the pike position

canonicalName: Ankle Driver (standing knee drive, 5 s hold)
equipment: one vertical rack upright post beside her, held with both hands for balance; nothing else
panel1: Standing in a split stance facing the post, hands holding it, the front foot flat, the front knee directly above the front ankle, the back leg straight with its heel lifted
panel2: Same stance and hold, but the FRONT knee is driven far forward well past the front toes while the front heel stays flat on the floor, held
delta: in panel 2 the front knee is driven far forward past the toes while the front heel stays down
primary: Calf and soleus of the front leg (lengthened)
paintOn: the back of the lower leg of the front leg
doNotPaint: the back leg, thighs, arms, torso
muscleSource: USMS article (ankle mobility section) + linked 'Ankle Drivers' demonstration video; ankle dorsiflexion stretch of the soleus/gastrocnemius
poseRefNote: this photo shows the split stance holding a rack

equipment: a plain dark grey exercise mat only, no other equipment
panel1: Seated upright on the mat in the 90/90 position: the front leg bent 90 degrees at the knee with that shin lying across in front of her body, the back leg bent 90 degrees with that shin pointing out to the side behind her, both knees on the mat, torso tall, fingertips lightly on the mat
primary: Gluteus maximus and deep hip external rotators of the front leg (lengthened)
paintOn: the outer hip and buttock of the front leg
doNotPaint: the back leg, thighs' fronts, arms, torso
muscleSource: USMS article (hips section) + linked '90:90 Hip Hold' demonstration video
poseRefNote: this photo shows the 90/90 seated position

equipment: exactly ONE football (soccer ball) under her feet; nothing else
panel1: Reverse tabletop: sitting facing up, hands flat on the floor behind her shoulders, hips lifted so thighs and torso form a straight line, knees bent about 90 degrees, both heels resting together on top of the football placed close to her hips
panel2: Same reverse tabletop with hips still lifted, but the football has rolled further away under her feet so her legs are much straighter, heels still on top of the ball
delta: in panel 2 the ball has rolled further away and her legs are much straighter while her hips stay lifted
paintOn: both buttocks and the back of both thighs
muscleSource: FIFA 11+ for Kids manual (F-MARC, 2016) p.50, Exercise 6 Spiderman: 'Focus: strengthening the core muscles and the hamstrings... keep your backside up and tense your stomach and back'; Level 5 'Ball bearing' illustration
poseRefNote: this illustration shows the position with the feet on the ball

equipment: a plain dark grey exercise mat only, no other equipment
panel1: On hands and knees with the knees spread VERY wide apart (much wider than the hips), shins parallel to each other pointing straight back, inner edges of the feet on the mat
panel2: Same very wide knees and parallel shins, she has lowered onto her forearms and pushed her hips back toward her heels, inner thighs close to the mat
delta: in panel 2 she is down on her forearms with her hips pushed far back between her wide knees
paintOn: the inner thighs of both legs
doNotPaint: arms, back, front of the thighs
muscleSource: Standard yoga/mobility frog stretch; adductor lengthening with hip abduction

equipment: a plain dark grey exercise mat only, no other equipment
panel1: Lying on her side: the top knee bent 90 degrees and pulled up in front of her hips, resting on the mat and held down by her bottom hand; the bottom leg bent behind her with its foot held by her top hand; chest facing sideways
panel2: Same leg holds, but she has rotated her upper back open so her chest faces the ceiling and her top shoulder is down near the mat
delta: in panel 2 her chest has rotated open to face the ceiling while both legs stay held
rotation: her chest faces sideways, the same way as her bent top knee
her chest faces straight up at the ceiling
primary: Thoracic rotation with hip flexors and quadriceps of the back leg (lengthened)
paintOn: the front of the thigh of the bent back leg
muscleSource: USMS article (hips section) + linked 'Brettzel' demonstration video
poseRefNote: this photo shows the opened Brettzel position

equipment: one low plyo box (about shin height); nothing else
panel1: Standing tall on ONE leg on top of the low box, the other leg held straight out in FRONT of the box, foot hovering in the air
panel2: The standing knee bends and travels far forward over the toes while the standing heel stays down on the box, lowering until the heel of the front free leg lightly taps the floor in front of the box
delta: in panel 2 her standing knee is bent far forward over her toes and the free heel touches the floor in front of the box
paintOn: the front of the thigh of the standing leg on the box
doNotPaint: the free leg held in front, arms, torso
muscleSource: Patrick (ATG) step-down, Rob Jackson's Strength Series B (Play AFL PDF) lists it by name; standard knee-over-toe quadriceps drill

panel1: Standing on the balls of both feet, heels just off the floor, knees almost straight, arms relaxed at her sides
panel2: Bounced straight up: both feet clearly OFF the floor with a visible gap and a shadow below them, legs straight, ankles pointed, arms at her sides
delta: in panel 2 both feet are clearly in the air with a visible gap and shadow under them
paintOn: the back of both lower legs
muscleSource: Standard plyometric pogo hop; ankle-stiffness calf drill (Rob Jackson movement prep, Somax runner programs)

equipment: exactly ONE foam roller; a mat
panel1: Face down propped on her forearms, the foam roller under the very top of both thighs just below the hips, legs straight
panel2: Same position, she has rolled forward so the roller is now just above her knees
delta: the roller is under the top of her thighs in panel 1 and just above her knees in panel 2
muscleSource: USMS article 'Top-down foam rolling' + linked demonstration video
poseRefNote: this photo shows foam rolling the front of the thighs

equipment: a plain dark grey exercise mat only, no other equipment
panel1: Lying on her back, knees bent, feet flat near her hips, hands planted flat on the mat beside her EARS with fingers pointing toward her shoulders and elbows pointing up
panel2: Pressed up into a full backbend: arms straight, hands and feet flat on the mat, hips and chest lifted high so her body forms a tall arch, head hanging between her arms
delta: she lies flat in panel 1 and is pushed up into a tall arch on straight arms in panel 2
primary: Hip flexors and front of the torso (lengthened)
paintOn: the front of both hips and the abdomen

canonicalName: Leg Tuck and Twist (Army PRT CD1)
equipment: a plain dark grey exercise mat only, no other equipment
panel1: Seated leaning back 45 degrees, arms straight with hands flat on the mat behind her, legs straight and together held a hand-width above the mat
panel2: Knees drawn up together toward the shoulder nearest the camera, rolled onto that buttock, legs tucked, hands still on the mat behind her
delta: her legs are straight and low in panel 1 and tucked with both knees toward one shoulder in panel 2
rotation: her chest faces forward toward her straight legs
her chest still faces forward while her hips and knees have turned toward the camera
paintOn: the abdomen and the side of the waist
muscleSource: FM 7-22 Army Physical Readiness Training (2012) p.9-9, Conditioning Drill 1 Exercise 4 'Leg tuck and twist': develops trunk strength and mobility
poseRefNote: this figure shows the starting position and Count 1 (knees tucked toward one shoulder)

equipment: a plain dark grey exercise mat only, no other equipment
panel1: Standing with feet very wide, front foot turned out, both legs straight, arms out level at shoulder height
panel2: Front knee bent 90 degrees over the front ankle, the lower forearm resting on the front thigh, the other arm reaching straight overhead past the ear so the body forms one long diagonal line from the back foot to the top hand
delta: in panel 2 her front knee is bent and her top arm and body form one long diagonal from the back foot
primary: Quadriceps and gluteus of the bent front leg
paintOn: the front of the thigh and the buttock of the bent front leg
muscleSource: Standard yoga pose; front-leg knee flexion under load

equipment: a plain dark grey exercise mat only, no other equipment
panel1: On hands and knees, hands under shoulders, knees under hips, back flat
panel2: The leg nearest the camera kicked straight back and up until it is in line with her back, knee straight, the other knee stays on the mat
delta: in panel 2 the near leg is kicked straight back level with her back
primary: Gluteus maximus of the kicking leg
paintOn: the buttock of the kicking leg
muscleSource: Bliss et al. 2021 (J Sport Exerc Sci) golf RAMP warm-up: 'Single leg kneeling kickbacks x10 each side' (bodyweight activation)
mustNot: no dumbbell, no band, not a triceps kickback

equipment: exactly TWO gymnastic rings hanging low on straps in front of her, one in each hand
panel1: Kneeling upright on a mat, arms straight in front of her holding the two low rings at hip height, body straight from knees to head
panel2: Leaning her straight body forward from the knees while her straight arms slide the rings forward and up above her head, body one long line from knees to hands, nearly horizontal
delta: she kneels upright in panel 1 and leans far forward with her arms extended overhead in panel 2

equipment: a plain dark grey exercise mat only, no other equipment
panel1: Lying on her back, arms by her sides, heels dug into the mat with the knees only slightly bent (legs much straighter than a normal bridge)
panel2: Same heel position, hips lifted off the mat and held so the body is a straight line from shoulders to heels
delta: her hips are on the mat in panel 1 and lifted in a straight line in panel 2
muscleSource: Rob Jackson's Strength Maintenance Level 1/2 (Play AFL PDF + linked video): 'Hamstring holds' / 'Single leg hamstring holds' - isometric long-lever hamstring bridge
